newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Newspaper links Suharto, family to Astra.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper links Suharto, family to Astra.

text.p: An Indonesian newspaper reported on Friday that President Suharto's daugther Siti Hardianti Rukmana was in negotiations to buy out the largest shareholder of automobile conglomerate Astra International.
Bisnis Indonesia daily said also that a group to which Suharto and his eldest son had links was in separate negotiations for a stake in the company, Indonesia's largest vehicle manufacturer.
The report could not be independently confirmed.
The newspaper quoted an unamed source as saying Rukmana held negotiations on Thursday with Prajogo Pangestu, the chairman of the Barito Group, to buy out his 10.68 percent stake in Astra.

The newspaper said the Nusamba Group, led by another timber tycoon, Muhammad (Bob) Hasan, was also in negotiations to buy a stake in Astra from the chairman of tobacco conglomerate PT H.M. Sampoerna, Putra Sampoerna.

Putra Sampoerna said earlier this week that he had recently bought some shares in Astra but refused to give details on the quantity or price. Bisnis Indonesia put his holding in Astra at about five percent.
The Nusamba Group is 80 percent owned by three foundations controlled by Suharto with the balance held by the president's son Sigit Hardjojudanto and Hasan, each with 10 percent.

The newspaper quoted the unnamed source as saying Nusamba was also likely to buy another 10.61 percent stake in Astra which was currently owned by government-related pension funds and state-owned banks.
Astra shares have risen sharply since the beginning of last week on what brokers have said could be a takeover bid in the making.
The company's holdings are widely scattered with Pangestu holding the largest stake followed by Toyota Motor Corp, which owns 8.26 percent.

Suharto was reported to have met Astra's president commissioner A.R. Ramly on Wednesday in his capacity as a member of the Prominent Person Group of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
Ramly declined to reveal details of the meeting.
Astra was trading at around 3,750 rupiah in early trading on Friday, up from 2,625 on September 16.
